canonicalFacts.claim: Gout is caused by monosodium urate crystal deposition in joints and tissues
Risk factors include male sex, obesity, hypertension, alcohol intake, diuretic use, diet rich in meat and seafood, and chronic kidney disease
Acute gout inflammation is mediated by NLRP3 inflammasome activation leading to IL-1β release
Diagnosis can be confirmed by identification of monosodium urate crystals in synovial fluid
Up to one-third of chronic kidney disease patients have a history of gout
Patients with gout have increased risk of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Limit consumption of purine-rich foods including organ meats and shellfish
Reduce alcohol consumption, particularly beer and spirits
Maintain healthy weight and address obesity
Follow dietary approaches that address cardiometabolic comorbidities holistically

redFlags: Febuxostat may increase cardiovascular mortality compared to allopurinol in patients with cardiovascular disease
Less than 25% of gout patients with chronic kidney disease achieve target serum urate levels
Multiple drug interactions and dosing adjustments required in patients with kidney disease

excludedAgents.name: febuxostat
excludedAgents.reason: showed no benefit over placebo for kidney function preservation in stage 3 CKD patients with asymptomatic hyperuricemia

excludedAgents.name: DKB114
excludedAgents.reason: showed no significant difference from placebo in reducing serum uric acid levels after 6 weeks in patients with asymptomatic hyperuricemia
